summary: Make mesh validity inspectable: combinatorial manifoldness, consistent orientation and geometric self-intersection are three different questions.
objective: Build a mesh inspector that highlights non-manifold edges, inconsistently oriented faces and self-intersections as separate findings.
intent_signals: Check whether a mesh is closed, manifold and consistently oriented.
Show why a mesh can look fine and still be invalid for boolean operations.
example_prompts: Build a mesh validity inspector that separates non-manifold edges from self-intersections.
Show a mesh with flipped faces and let me repair the orientation.
negative_signals: Not a repair pipeline: this recipe reports findings and may reorient faces, but it does not claim to fix arbitrary meshes.
Not a rendering quality check; shading artefacts are a symptom, not the subject.
not_for: Not a repair pipeline: this recipe reports findings and may reorient faces, but it does not claim to fix arbitrary meshes.
Not a rendering quality check; shading artefacts are a symptom, not the subject.

entities.name: Inspected mesh
entities.guidance: Load or build a mesh with deliberate defects and keep face and edge indices addressable, since findings are reported per element.

entities.name: Finding overlays
entities.guidance: Give each finding class its own overlay: boundary edges, non-manifold edges, inconsistently oriented faces and self-intersecting triangles.

entities.name: Normal display
entities.guidance: Draw face normals as short spikes so a flipped face is visible as geometry rather than only as shading.

state_contract.model: An indexed mesh with per-edge incidence counts, per-face winding relative to neighbours, a vertex-link connectivity test that detects non-manifold vertices, and a self-intersection test. Findings are lists of element indices per class: boundary edge, non-manifold edge, non-manifold vertex, inconsistent winding, non-orientable component and self-intersecting face.
state_contract.authority: The element lists are authoritative. A repair action must rebuild them, and a stale overlay after an edit is a defect.
actions: Run the validity check and step through findings.
Toggle each finding overlay and the normal spikes.

invariants: An edge shared by more than two faces is reported as non-manifold even when the mesh looks closed.
Consistent orientation is a combinatorial property and does not by itself imply the absence of self-intersections.
Reorientation changes face winding only: vertex positions and mesh topology are identical before and after, and a component that cannot be consistently oriented keeps its original winding.

Edge counts alone do not certify a 2-manifold: two tetrahedral surfaces joined at a single shared vertex have two faces per edge and consistent winding, and are reported through the vertex-link test instead.
Reorientation can fail: a component that is non-orientable, such as a Moebius strip, is reported as a conflict rather than repaired by flipping windings.
motion_guidance: Animate a camera move to each finding rather than teleporting, so the viewer keeps spatial context.
Flash a repaired face once and then leave it in its final state; a persistent animation hides whether the finding is resolved.
known_limits: Self-intersection tests are geometric and tolerance-sensitive near coincident faces.
This recipe describes checks; performance on large meshes depends entirely on the implementation chosen.
The declared defect classes are edge manifoldness, vertex-link manifoldness, winding consistency, orientability and self-intersection; anything outside that list is not evaluated.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: A polygon mesh treated as a surface is required to be a consistent and orientable surface mesh with the topology of a two-manifold.
claims.scope: Combinatorial definition used by the cited library documentation.

source_refs.locator: Polygon Mesh Processing, polygon mesh definition

claims.statement: These requirements are mostly combinatorial and do not prevent defects such as self-intersections or degenerate faces and edges.
claims.scope: Explicit separation of combinatorial validity from geometric validity, as documented.

source_refs.locator: Polygon Mesh Processing, note on combinatorial requirements

object_craft.structure: Flat-shaded faces with visible edges so topology is readable; avoid smoothing that hides seams and duplicate vertices.
object_craft.material: Neutral grey mesh so every finding overlay stands out; reserve saturated colour entirely for findings.
object_craft.articulation: None. Only overlays and, on repair, face winding change.

object_craft.structure: Edge tubes and face patches slightly offset from the surface so they do not z-fight with the mesh.
object_craft.material: One accent per finding class with distinct dash or hatch patterns so classes are distinguishable in monochrome.
object_craft.articulation: Overlays rebuild after every check or repair.

physical_contract.scope: Static geometric and combinatorial analysis; no simulation.
checks: Vertex positions are unchanged after a reorientation repair.
A mesh with a triple edge is reported as non-manifold even when it is watertight by appearance.
